label: benign
description: Arabic and Hebrew sentences that use the LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK (U+200E) to keep an embedded Latin term, acronym, filename, or bracketed phrase reading in the right direction. This is the mirror image of the directional marks in rtl-with-bidi-controls and a real, common practice in mixed-direction text.

cases.title: Arabic sentence isolating a Latin browser name with LRM
cases.text: افتح الرابط في المتصفح‎ Chrome ثم أكمل عملية التسجيل.
cases.rationale: An LRM before the Latin product name keeps it left-to-right inside the Arabic sentence; because the text contains real Arabic letters the directional-mark signal stays silent and this is a true negative (score 0).

cases.title: Hebrew line bracketed with LRM around an English acronym
cases.text: המערכת תומכת ב‎REST‎ ובפורמט JSON בלבד.
cases.rationale: Two LRMs fence an English acronym so it is not reordered by the surrounding Hebrew; legitimate mixed-direction typography, and the detector scores it zero.

cases.title: Arabic report with an LRM-fenced parenthetical
cases.text: كتب في التقرير ‎(approved)‎ ثم أرسله إلى الفريق.
cases.rationale: LRMs around a bracketed English word keep the parentheses upright in the Arabic paragraph, a standard fix that the detector correctly ignores (score 0).

cases.title: Hebrew sentence with LRM around a Latin filename
cases.text: עדכן את הקובץ report‎.docx לפני הדדליין.
cases.rationale: An LRM stops the file extension from jumping in the Hebrew sentence; a real typographic need, and the case is a true negative.

cases.title: Arabic release note fencing a version string with LRM
cases.rationale: LRMs hold a version string left-to-right inside Arabic prose, the correct use of a directional mark; the detector stays silent.

cases.title: Hebrew sentence with LRM around a quoted English word
cases.rationale: LRMs around an English quotation keep the quote marks in place within the Hebrew line; a legitimate mark and a true negative (score 0).
